title: Swim at Streets Beach, a lagoon in the middle of Brisbane
description: A free man-made sand beach and lagoon on the river opposite the CBD, left over from World Expo 88.

title: Hold a koala at Lone Pine, the world's first koala sanctuary
description: Opened in 1927 and still the largest koala sanctuary anywhere - reachable by river cruise from the city.

title: Watch the city light up from Mount Coot-tha
description: Brisbane's lookout hill, with the botanic gardens, a planetarium and the whole city grid laid out below at dusk.

title: Ride the free CityHopper ferry along the Brisbane River
description: A completely free ferry looping between Sydney Street and North Quay - the cheapest river cruise in Australia.

title: Eat your way through the shipping containers at Eat Street Northshore
description: A riverside night market built from around 180 repurposed shipping containers, open Friday to Sunday evenings.

title: See a contemporary show at GOMA
description: The largest modern art gallery in Australia, free to enter, and home to the Asia Pacific Triennial.

title: Watch the Crocoseum show at Australia Zoo
description: The Irwin family zoo at Beerwah, built around a 5,000-seat stadium for crocodile and free-flight bird demonstrations.

title: Road-trip the Sunshine Coast from Caloundra to Noosa
description: An hour north of Brisbane - surf beaches, a volcanic hinterland and a noticeably slower pace than the Gold Coast.

title: Have breakfast on Hastings Street at Noosa Heads
description: Queensland's most polished beach town, where the main street runs straight onto a north-facing swimming beach.

title: Find the wild koalas on the Noosa National Park coastal track
description: A 5.4km headland walk past Tea Tree Bay and Hells Gates, with koalas in the trees near Tea Tree and dolphins offshore.

title: Learn to surf on the gentle break at Noosa Main Beach
description: One of very few north-facing beaches on the east coast, which makes it unusually calm and ideal for a first lesson.

title: Drive the Glass House Mountains lookout circuit
description: Thirteen volcanic plugs rising abruptly from the plain, named by Cook in 1770 and deeply significant to the Jinibara and Kabi Kabi peoples.

title: Climb Mount Ngungun at sunrise
description: The most achievable of the Glass House peaks - 2.8km return to a ledge looking straight across at Tibrogargan and Beerwah.

title: Walk the Mooloolaba Spit at first light
description: A patrolled beach, an esplanade of cafes and a trawler harbour where you can buy prawns straight off the boat.

title: Swim the calm passage water at Bulcock Beach, Caloundra
description: Sheltered behind Bribie Island, with a tidal current that locals ride like a lazy river on the run-out.

title: See the Gold Coast skyline from the water
description: 57km of surf beach backed by high-rises and canal estates - Australia's most unapologetic holiday city.

title: Look down from the SkyPoint observation deck at Surfers Paradise
description: Level 77 of Q1, and the Climb takes you outside to 270m - the tallest external building climb in the country.

title: Watch the point break from the Burleigh headland at sunset
description: A world-class right-hand point break, a headland national park full of brush turkeys, and the best sunset view back up the coast.

title: Walk the Twin Falls circuit at Springbrook
description: Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage on the rim of an ancient volcano - a 4km track that goes behind two waterfalls.

title: See the glow worms in the cave at Natural Bridge
description: A waterfall pouring through the roof of a basalt cave, whose ceiling fills with glow worms after dark.

title: Walk the treetop canopy bridges at O'Reilly's
description: Ancient Antarctic beech forest on the caldera rim, with 160km of track and a suspended boardwalk 15m up in the canopy.

title: Walk the Tamborine Rainforest Skywalk
description: A plateau of rainforest, wineries and galleries forty minutes from the coast, with a 300m steel walkway through the canopy.

title: Step into the man-made Glow Worm Caves at Tamborine
description: A purpose-built cave housing a glow worm colony, so you can see them in daylight hours and in any weather.

title: Get mobbed by lorikeets at the Currumbin morning feed
description: A not-for-profit sanctuary running a wildlife hospital, famous for the wild rainbow lorikeet feeding twice a day.

title: Ride the DC Rivals HyperCoaster at Movie World
description: Home to the tallest, longest and fastest roller coaster in the Southern Hemisphere, plus a daily parade.

title: Take on the Giant Drop at Dreamworld
description: Australia's largest theme park, with a serious thrill-ride lineup and a genuine tiger conservation program on site.

title: Drop through the Kamikaze at Wet'n'Wild
description: A huge water park on the Pacific Motorway, heated in winter, with a wave pool and a dive-in cinema.

title: Balance under the Pyramid boulders at Girraween
description: Enormous granite domes and precariously balanced boulders in Queensland's cold high country, near the wineries of Stanthorpe.

title: Drive the beach highway on K'gari
description: Formerly Fraser Island - the largest sand island on earth, where the beach is a gazetted road and only 4WDs get on. Butchulla country.

title: Swim in the pure silica sand of Lake McKenzie
description: A perched dune lake sitting on compacted sand and leaves, holding rainwater so pure almost nothing can live in it.

title: Float down Eli Creek on K'gari
description: Four million litres an hour of crystal clear freshwater running to the sea - walk up the boardwalk and float back down.

title: Photograph the rusting Maheno on Seventy-Five Mile Beach
description: A former luxury liner and WWI hospital ship blown ashore by a cyclone in 1935 and slowly disappearing into the sand.

title: Walk the Urangan Pier at Hervey Bay
description: A 868m pier left from an old sugar and timber jetty, on a bay so sheltered it has no surf at all.

title: Have a humpback swim up to the boat in Hervey Bay
description: The world's first Whale Heritage Site - humpbacks stop here to rest with their calves, and often come to inspect the boats.

title: Tour the Bundaberg Rum distillery
description: Distilling since 1888 from the region's sugar cane molasses - the tour ends in the barrel house and the tasting bar.

title: Watch a loggerhead turtle nest at Mon Repos
description: The largest loggerhead nesting concentration in the South Pacific - ranger-guided night visits, November to March. Book ahead.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Lady Elliot Island
description: A coral cay at the southern tip of the Great Barrier Reef, reached by light plane, with resident manta rays year-round.

title: Snorkel the lagoon at Lady Musgrave Island
description: A coral cay ringed by a 3,000-hectare lagoon you can boat right into - camping is allowed, with a permit and all your own water.

title: Surf the northernmost surf beach on the east coast at Agnes Water
description: The Great Barrier Reef blocks swell everywhere north of here, so this is the last real surf beach on the Queensland coast.

title: Watch the sun set over the water at the Town of 1770
description: Named for Cook's second Australian landing, and one of the only spots on the east coast where you watch the sun set into the sea.

title: Straddle the Tropic of Capricorn marker at Rockhampton
description: The beef capital of Australia, sitting exactly on the Tropic of Capricorn, with a spire on the highway marking the line.

title: Hear a choir sing in the Cathedral Cave at Capricorn Caves
description: Privately run limestone caves with famous acoustics, and a chamber where a shaft of sunlight lands only near the summer solstice.

title: Swim the Yeppoon foreshore lagoon
description: The Capricorn Coast's main beach town, with a free stinger-safe lagoon on the foreshore and Keppel Bay islands offshore.

title: Snorkel straight off the sand at Great Keppel Island
description: Seventeen beaches and fringing coral you can swim to from shore, thirty minutes by ferry and far quieter than the Whitsundays.

title: Take the Cape Hillsborough sunrise kangaroo walk near Mackay
description: Wallabies and kangaroos come onto the beach at dawn to feed on mangrove pods - one of the most photographed sunrises in Queensland.

title: Walk the rainforest at Eungella, an island of forest in the dry
description: Rainforest isolated from the coast for thousands of years, with species found nowhere else, an hour inland from Mackay.

title: Wait for a platypus at Broken River, Eungella
description: Purpose-built viewing platforms over a clear river, and the single most reliable place in Australia to see a wild platypus.

title: Base yourself at Airlie Beach for the Whitsundays
description: The mainland gateway to the islands, with a free stinger-safe lagoon and a marina full of sailing boats going out for two nights.

title: Sail the Whitsundays for two nights
description: 74 islands inside the Great Barrier Reef, sheltered enough to sail comfortably and close enough together to anchor somewhere new each night.

title: Walk the length of Whitehaven Beach
description: 7km of 98% pure silica sand that stays cool underfoot in full sun and squeaks as you walk.

title: See the swirling sand from the Hill Inlet lookout
description: The tide pushes white silica and blue water into shifting marbled patterns at the northern end of Whitehaven - go at low tide.

title: Climb Passage Peak on Hamilton Island
description: The most developed Whitsunday island, but a 2.9km climb to 239m gets you above all of it for a view over the whole group.

title: Walk the Living Reef coral lagoon at Daydream Island
description: A small resort island with a free-form outdoor coral lagoon running through the middle of it, holding around 100 species.

title: Swim the Cairns Esplanade Lagoon
description: The launching point for the reef and the Daintree - the town beach is mudflat, so the free saltwater lagoon is where everyone swims.

title: Watch the wading birds on the Cairns Esplanade mudflats
description: An internationally recognised shorebird site - migratory waders arrive from Siberia and Alaska every summer, right beside the boardwalk.

title: Dive the Great Barrier Reef
description: The largest living structure on earth, 2,300km long and visible from space - outer reef sites are far better than the inner ones.

title: Snorkel off the sand at Green Island
description: A true coral cay with rainforest growing on it, 45 minutes from Cairns, where the reef starts a few metres off the beach.

title: Visit the turtle rehabilitation centre on Fitzroy Island
description: A continental island of rainforest and coral beaches, with a volunteer-run turtle hospital and a good climb to the lighthouse.

title: Swim at Four Mile Beach in Port Douglas
description: The comfortable base between the reef and the Daintree. Stinger nets go up from November to May - swim inside them.

title: Stand in the oldest surviving rainforest on earth
description: Around 180 million years old and continuously forested since - Kuku Yalanji country, and the only place the reef meets rainforest.

title: Stand where the rainforest meets the reef at Cape Tribulation
description: Two World Heritage areas touching at one beach. Do not swim - this is estuarine crocodile and stinger country.

title: Take a Dreamtime walk at Mossman Gorge
description: Kuku Yalanji guides lead a smoking ceremony and bush tucker walk through the gorge - the swimming holes are cold and clear.

title: Browse the Kuranda village markets in the rainforest
description: A village on the Atherton escarpment reached by train one way and cable car the other, with markets running since the 1970s.

title: Ride the Kuranda Scenic Railway past Barron Falls
description: An 1891 line hand-cut through 15 tunnels and 37 bridges up the escarpment, stopping at the Barron Falls lookout.

title: Glide over the canopy on the Skyrail Rainforest Cableway
description: 7.5km of gondola metres above World Heritage rainforest, with boardwalk stops on the way - take a glass-floor car.

title: Do the waterfall circuit on the Atherton Tablelands
description: Cool volcanic highlands behind Cairns - crater lakes, dairy country, and a 17km loop linking three swimmable waterfalls.

title: Swim under Millaa Millaa Falls
description: The most photographed waterfall in Australia - an 18m curtain into a round swimming hole, with a shampoo ad filmed here.

title: Explore the ruined Spanish castle at Paronella Park
description: A Catalan immigrant built a mock castle, ballroom and tunnels in the rainforest in the 1930s, powered by his own hydro plant. Now a ruin, lit at night.

title: Look for a cassowary at Mission Beach
description: 14km of palm-backed beach and the best chance in Australia of seeing a wild southern cassowary. Keep your distance - they are dangerous.

title: Stand at the base of Wallaman Falls
description: Australia's highest single-drop waterfall at 268m, with a steep 3.2km track down to the plunge pool and back.

title: Dive the SS Yongala wreck out of Townsville
description: A 1911 shipwreck 90m down the coast, considered one of the best wreck dives in the world - advanced certification required.

title: Walk up Castle Hill in the middle of Townsville
description: A 286m pink granite monolith rising out of the suburbs, walked daily by half the city before the heat comes up.

title: Find wild koalas on the Forts Walk, Magnetic Island
description: WWII gun emplacements at the top of a 4km walk, through one of the densest wild koala populations in northern Australia.

title: Hire a topless Barbie car at Nelly Bay
description: The Magnetic Island ferry terminal, where the local tradition is hiring a brightly coloured open-top Moke to do the island loop.

title: Feed a cassowary at Billabong Sanctuary
description: A small eco-certified wildlife park south of Townsville built around a natural billabong, with hands-on keeper sessions all day.

title: Walk the gold-boom streets of Charters Towers
description: Once so rich it was called The World, with its own stock exchange - the grand arcade and verandahs are still standing.

title: Walk inside the Undara lava tubes
description: Among the longest lava tube systems from a single volcano on earth, formed 190,000 years ago - guided access only.

title: See the Curtain Fig Tree near Atherton
description: A strangler fig that toppled into a neighbouring tree and dropped a 15m curtain of aerial roots - reached by a short boardwalk.

title: Climb Grassy Hill at Cooktown where Cook beached the Endeavour
description: The Endeavour was repaired here for 48 days in 1770 - the town holds both that history and strong Guugu Yimithirr presence.

title: Drive to the Tip of Cape York
description: The northernmost point of mainland Australia - a serious 4WD expedition with river crossings, only passable in the dry season.
